findings.claim:
This extends the coordinator's item (c). The 8–12 px growth is confirmed, and its cause and a verified two-line fix are below.

Cause:
- C6g-2 changed '.sr-say' to 'position: relative !important; display: block; height: 1px; margin: -1px 0 0'. It also dropped 'clip', which only applies to absolutely positioned boxes. This is no longer the standard out-of-flow visually-hidden rule.
- #namerow-say therefore became an in-flow child of '#pdp .gallery', which is 'display: grid; gap: 12px' (and 'gap: 8px !important' up to 700 wide).
- Every in-flow child of a grid is a grid item, so the region gets its own row track. That track is 0 px (1 px minus the 1 px margin), but the grid inserts one more row gap before the note.

Effect, in every view of every product page:
- 'Pictures are renders. Nothing is built yet.' sits 32 px under the thumbnails or names row instead of 20 from 701 wide.
- Up to 700 wide it sits 16 px under instead of 8, double OLD's spacing.
- The gallery and everything under it move down 12 or 8 px. The upright-tablet bar thresholds move with them.

A negative margin on the region itself cannot win the space back. I tried it and still got +12 and +8, because a grid track never goes below 0 px.

The region is invisible and the row itself is unchanged.

findings.claim:
Screen-reader reality of the 1.5 s hold.

What the hold achieves:
- During the 1.5 s, a browse-mode reader meets the names twice: the row's links, then 'Tropos in Acid, Hemisphere in Ember, ...'. In-page find counts them twice.
- After that, both happen once.

Is emptying that early safe?
- NVDA: safe. Its in-process hook copies the live text when the event fires.
- VoiceOver: uncertain. Chrome on macOS only posts NSAccessibilityLiveRegionChangedNotification, and VoiceOver then reads the region itself. When it does that is not documented.
- After a thumbnail click VoiceOver is busy saying the tab ('At the bar, selected, tab, 5 of 6' takes 1.5-2.5 s). If it reads the region lazily, the text may already be gone.
- I ran no screen reader, so none of this is verified on real assistive technology.

Is there a better standard pattern?
- Marking the region aria-hidden after it speaks is not better. Find-in-page still counts the text. The region would also have to be re-exposed and then filled after a delay on every view change, because some browser and screen-reader pairs miss changes to a region that has only just been exposed.
- Clearing only on the next change is C6f's behavior, with the duplicate the C6f gate reported.
- Keep NEW's pattern. Raise the hold to about 5-7 s (React Aria uses 7 s) only if a VoiceOver test on macOS Safari, macOS Chrome or iOS Safari loses or cuts the names. The cost is a longer stretch where browse mode meets the names twice.
